notes: Built from the PDF alone (02-20000-48, Reviewed 05/28/26, Revised 06/15/26). The download holds a single clean copy; no redline. Original Effective Date 07/01/15 is recorded as effective_date; 06/15/26 is the latest revision ('Review; no change in position statement').

Pathways: one per indication the position statement grants coverage for: thoracic deformity fusion, lumbar deformity fusion, discectomy, laminectomy for stenosis, laminectomy for a space-occupying lesion, nine lumbar fusion diagnoses (the document's 'any of the following' list, each a bullet group), and lumbar total disc arthroplasty.

Code mapping. Fusion (22533, 22534, 22558, 22585, 22612, 22614, 22630, 22632, 22633, 22634): both deformity pathways and all nine fusion-by-diagnosis pathways; the weakest-of-several rule means a chart passes if any one diagnosis pathway is met. Discectomy (63030, 63035, 63042, 63044, 63056, 63057): 63030/63035 describe laminotomy with excision of a herniated disc, 63042/63044 are the re-exploration versions and 63056/63057 the transpedicular approach for a far-lateral herniated disc. Laminectomy (63005, 63012, 63017, 63047, 63048, 63052, 63053, plus 63030, 63035, 63042, 63044): the section heading is 'Lumbar Laminectomy (Laminotomy, Facetectomy, Foraminotomy)' so the laminotomy codes 63030-63044 are governed by both the discectomy and the laminectomy pathways, since the same CPT covers foraminotomy for stenosis and disc excision; 63052/63053 are laminectomy during posterior interbody arthrodesis and follow the laminectomy pathways. TDA (22857, 22860): the arthroplasty pathway. 0164T, 0165T, 22862, 22865 (removal / revision of an artificial disc) are in the table with no criteria anywhere in the document; mapped to the arthroplasty pathway as the closest section rather than left ungoverned.

Every code in the table is tagged covered: the document states no code or exactly-described procedure as non-covered or investigational. The fusion exclusions are by sole indication, not by code, so the fusion codes stay covered and the exclusions carry no codes.

The ++ block 'Conservative nonsurgical therapy for lumbar spinal fusion should include the following' (analgesics, 6 weeks PT, cognitive/behavioral evaluation) is advisory wording ('should'), and the ++ marker is referenced nowhere else in the document. It is therefore not nested into the fusion pathways that say only 'conservative nonsurgical therapy' (idiopathic scoliosis, degenerative scoliosis, isthmic spondylolisthesis, recurrent herniation, adjacent-level disease). Where the document itself spells the three components out with 'that included' (spinal stenosis fusion item a, discectomy, laminectomy, total disc arthroplasty) they are leaves. A reviewer who reads the ++ definition as binding would add the three leaves to those five fusion pathways.

Parenthetical 'analgesics should include anti-inflammatory medications with or without adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants, unless contraindicated or not tolerated' is advisory and sits in the question, not the criterion text.

'Participation in at least 6 weeks of physical therapy (including active exercise) or documentation of why the candidate could not tolerate physical therapy' is an any of two leaves: the second half waives the first.
'Evaluation and appropriate management of associated cognitive, behavioral, or addiction issues, if any' is conditional: a chart with no such issues satisfies it.

Laminectomy 'Signs or symptoms of at least 1 of the following': the bullet 'Neurologic claudication that is persistent and refractory, OR persistent debilitating pain (...), that is refractory to at least 6 weeks of conservative nonsurgical therapy that included the following' is read as three alternatives: rapidly progressive deficits; persistent and refractory claudication; persistent debilitating pain refractory to 6 weeks of the listed therapy. The 6-week conservative-therapy block attaches to the pain clause only (the discectomy section has the identical construction with pain alone). A stricter reading would attach the 6-week block to the claudication clause too.

'At least 2 of the following' six radiculopathy signs is expanded to an any over all 15 pairs; 'any 2 of the following' four non-operative treatments to an any over 6 pairs. The header 'Signs and symptoms of radiculopathy on history and physical exam' is the label of that any, not a leaf, because the list defines it.

Deformity footnote: the bullet 'Failure of symptom or pain improvement upon completion of at least 12 weeks of focused non-operative care* in the past year' is the leaf (threshold 12 weeks = 2.77 months); the * definition ('Documented failure of at least twelve (12) consecutive weeks in the past year of any 2 of the following physician-directed conservative treatments') is the label of the any-of-pairs beneath it, so 'consecutive' and 'physician-directed' are carried in the label and question rather than as a second leaf stating the same 12 weeks.

The deformity emergency bullet is split in two: the deficit/weakness/paralysis and the 'corresponding evidence of spinal cord or nerve root compression on an MRI or CT scan images'. The trailing 'immediate surgical evaluation is indicated' is a consequence, not a requirement, and is left out.

'Imaging studies confirm spinal curvature and demonstrate at least one of the following' and 'Imaging studies that correspond to clinical findings and show at least one of the following' each hold a requirement of their own, so each is an all of a header leaf plus the any of measurements.

Fusion for spinal stenosis is read as all of: spinal stenosis; one of (spondylolisthesis on plain x-rays, instability on imaging, instability anticipated from bilateral/wide decompression); and either a or b. Item a is split into claudication/radicular pain with functional impairment, stenosis documented on MRI or other imaging, failed at least 3 months of conservative therapy, and the three therapy components printed under it (flat, as printed).

Degenerative scoliosis header 'with a minimum Cobb angle of 30°, or significant sagittal imbalance (eg, sagittal vertical axis >5 cm), and with any one of the following' is read as scoliosis AND (Cobb >= 30° OR sagittal imbalance) AND one of the three symptom items. The '>5 cm' is an example ('eg') of significant imbalance and is kept as the threshold.

'Documented progression of deformity with persistent axial (nonradiating) pain and impairment or loss of function unresponsive to at least 1 year of conservative nonsurgical therapy' and the neurogenic-symptoms item are each split into the clinical picture plus a shared 'unresponsive to at least 1 year of conservative nonsurgical therapy' leaf.

'Persistent back pain (with or without neurogenic symptoms), with impairment or loss of function' (isthmic) and 'Persistent back pain (with or without neurogenic symptoms) with impairment or loss of function' (adjacent-level) are the same requirement; one leaf with the isthmic wording serves both. 'Unresponsive to at least 3 months of conservative nonsurgical therapy' (isthmic, recurrent herniation, adjacent-level) and 'failed at least 3 months of conservative nonsurgical therapy' (stenosis, idiopathic scoliosis) are kept as two leaves because the verbatim wording differs, though they state the same trial. 'severe or rapidly progressive symptoms of motor loss, neurogenic claudication, or cauda equina syndrome' appears in five fusion sections and is one shared leaf.

'Recurrent, same-level disc herniation, at least 3 months after previous disc surgery' is two leaves: the recurrence and the 3-month interval (duration threshold). Pseudarthrosis 'Impairment or loss of function, in an individual who had experienced significant interval relief of prior symptoms' is two leaves: impairment (shared with recurrent herniation) and interval relief.

Instability: 'Instability due to fracture, dislocation, infection, abscess, or tumor when extensive surgery is required that could create an unstable spine' is read as two requirements (the cause of instability, and that extensive surgery is required that could create an unstable spine), an all. A reviewer could read the 'when' clause as explanatory and accept the first alone. Flatback likewise: the syndrome with sagittal imbalance AND fusion performed with osteotomy or interbody spacers.

Scoping leaves: the section headers 'Thoracic deformity (minimal / secondary / flexible lumbar involvement) in adults', 'Lumbar deformity (with or without secondary thoracic involvement) in adults' and discectomy 'for the treatment of lumbar herniated disc' name the population or diagnosis the pathway covers, so each is the first leaf of its pathway, as the fusion diagnoses ('Spinal stenosis', 'Isthmic spondylolisthesis', ...) are. 'adults' carries no number in the document, so no age threshold is typed.

'*Note: For multi-level fusion, criteria must be met for each level intended for fusion' is a rule about how to apply the pathways, not a chart requirement; it is recorded on each fusion pathway's notes.

Total disc arthroplasty: 'Candidate is age 18 to 60' is one leaf with threshold age >= 18 years; the 60-year upper bound is in the question (the schema holds one op per criterion). 'No more than Grade 1 spondylolisthesis' is typed as number <= 1 (grade). The contraindication list is 'including but not limited to'; the not(any) covers the nine listed items, each with its own leaf and threshold where printed (T-score <= -1.0, > 11 degrees, > 3mm). The FDA-approved-device requirement is kept answerable: a chart names the planned device and the surgeon's statement of on-label use.

Internal tension in the arthroplasty section (single level L3-4/L4-L5/L5-S1 in one bullet; one or two consecutive levels from L3-S1 in another; 'more than two levels' as a contraindication) is reproduced as printed, not resolved.

'within the past 6 months' on the two imaging requirements is typed as duration_months lte 6 (recency of the study); the app checks note dates only for 'at least' durations, so this is a hint, not a gate. Weeks convert at 12/52 (6 weeks = 1.38 months, 12 weeks = 2.77 months).

Fusion exclusions: the five sole-indication conditions are each an exclusion; the first carries the governing sentence (contiguous in the PDF), the others the condition as printed. They carry no codes because no code in the table is itself an excluded procedure. The Description and Summary and Analysis of Evidence sections state no requirements (the Scheuermann's kyphosis thresholds and the NASS recommendations there are evidence summary, not position) and are left out.

Program exceptions: FEP and SAO follow their own guidelines; Medicare Advantage products follow NCD 150.10 (Lumbar Artificial Disc Replacement) for the arthroplasty question. The Florida step-therapy exemption paragraph (627.42393) is a process statement and is left out. 'Related Guidelines: 02-20000-45, Cervical Spine Surgery' is cross-reference only.
